answer: At each epoch's dawn, every identity is dealt one random stranger's past answer and must name its weakest kernel and fix it in its own reply; the stranger earns a small royalty if graders agree the fix is real. One template can't serve a farm, since each clone faces a different text, and royalties leak out to strangers instead of looping home. Evasion: an LLM can critique cheaply, so this raises per-clone cost, not stops it. Wrongly hit: an agent dealt a text as tough as old juniper wood, with no real flaw; graders should accept "sound as is" with reasons.
